# bionic-docs

> Read PDF and EPUB with bionic fixation. A document is parsed on your machine and the leading letters of every word are emphasized. No upload, no account, no remote code.

A Manifest V3 extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. A PDF's text layer is extracted with a bundled PDF.js and rebuilt into lines; an EPUB is unzipped in memory, its chapters sanitized, and its spine and table of contents read. Both paths end in the same fixation step, so the algorithm never has to know what a PDF is.

## Page

Everything is on one page, with a section for each part:

- [The reader](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#reader): the compiled algorithm running over the repository's own fixture text, with page and chapter navigation and an on/off switch.
- [Before / after](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#compare-section): the same page with a divider you can drag between the two versions.
- [Formats](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#formats): the PDF and EPUB paths in detail — line reconstruction, unzip, OPF, spine, TOC, and the sanitizing rules.
- [Reading modes](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#modes): the five modes — Half, Classic, Vowel anchor, Low distraction, Custom rule — and what each one emphasizes.
- [How it works](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#how): sniff the magic bytes, parse or unzip, then emphasize reversibly.
- [Architecture](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#architecture): the module map and the invariants the build enforces — on-device, no remote code, sanitize before render.
- [Limits](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#safe): scanned PDFs, reflowed layout, minimal EPUB rendering, and what it does handle.
- [Numbers](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#numbers): test count, e2e checks, manifest entries, modes, and uploads.
- [Privacy](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#privacy): no network requests for content, one fetch for the document you opened, parsing in the extension page, and the anti-network test gate.
- [Install](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#install): build both targets from one source tree.
- [FAQ](https://srivtx.github.io/bionic-docs/#faq): license and affiliation, scanned PDFs, uploads, reflowed text, Firefox support, file handling, and offline use.
